modalities.name: Acupuncture & Electro-Acupuncture
modalities.description: Acupuncture consists of using very fine needles to stimulate certain points on the patient's body called acupoints along 14 channels through which Qi travels. Only sterilized disposable needles are used. Inserted painlessly to contact Qi (the sensation of Deqi). Regularly paired with infra-red lamps during the treatment session. Electro-acupuncture is offered for some treatments.
modalities.source_notes: Sterilized disposable stainless steel needles only. Disperses blockages in Qi flow.

modalities.name: Chinese Herbal Medicine
modalities.description: Rooted in a tradition dating back to the 1st century C.E. manual Shennong Bencao Jing (365 medicines). Places greater emphasis on the balance and interaction of many ingredients tailored to the specific condition of the patient. Offered in herbal powder, herbal pills, and nutritional supplements.
modalities.source_notes: Treats the patient as a complete person instead of just treating a specific sickness.

modalities.name: Huo Guan (Fire Cupping)
modalities.description: Traditional cupping therapy to relieve muscular tightness and clear stagnation.
modalities.source_notes: Offered as an add-on to acupuncture or standalone.

modalities.name: Gua Sha
modalities.description: Therapeutic scraping therapy used to relieve what is known in Chinese medicine as stagnation.

modalities.name: Chinese Medicine Massage
modalities.description: Acupressure and Chinese medicine massage appointments available during regular clinic hours and additional hours on Monday and Saturday.
modalities.source_notes: Additional hours open on Monday and Saturday for massage appointments.
